## Definition check

The section "Source rubric and schema paths (#158)" is present in my instructions, and the sentence beginning "Read release-specific notes" reads, verbatim and in full:

> Read release-specific notes from the dedicated `updates.update_details` field, `updates.description` or `notes`, requiring actual release or derivation information rather than crediting unrelated notes.

This is the current wording (it names the dedicated `updates.update_details` slot and forbids crediting unrelated notes), so I proceeded. Recorded `instrument_sha256` as `66ad6231…4864`, `instrument_kind: agent_definition`.

## Result: 36/50

| Basis | Score | Denominator |
|---|---|---|
| Normalized (N/A-adjusted) | **72.0%** | 36 / 50 |
| Fixed | **72.0%** | 36 / 50 |

`excluded_max_points: 0`, `sub_elements_not_applicable: 0` — no `applicable: false` items, so the two bases coincide.

**Applicability:** all five trigger conditions resolved as met, each on evidence outside the gated element. Human subjects via E1 `description`/`keywords` (ICU/PICU/NICU patient admissions) and E8 `collection_mechanisms`; datasets-shared via `distribution_formats`, `third_party_sharing.is_shared=true` and the August 2025 release (approval-gated access → ambiguity rule defaults to applicable); software-output via `external_resources` pointing at the chorus-ai repositories. E8.4 was scored on the #1081/#1082 rule — applicable because the data were processed, not because a repo is pointed at — and earned 1: OHNLP tokenization, chorus_waveform conversion, chorus-mapping and DeGauss each named software that transformed data actually in the release, not merely capture, hosting or validation tooling.

**Per element:** E1 3, E2 4, E3 4, E4 4, E5 3, E6 2, E7 5, E8 5, E9 4, E10 2.

**Drivers.** Strongest: funding transparency (grant `OT2OD032701` validates as NIH OT2/OD), processing provenance traceable to named repositories, and standards conformance stated consistently in four places. Weakest: Element 6 and Element 10 — a dataset that `status`, `distribution_dates` and `existing_uses` all describe as released and already cited in publications carries no DOI, version, citation or publisher. The two hardest calls were E4.1 and E4.2, both scored 1 on the governance-contact and tokenization evidence the sub-elements enumerate, with the missing IRB and the missing Safe Harbor/Expert Determination recorded as high- and medium-severity issues rather than double-counted. E4.4 (informed consent) scored 0: no consent, no waiver, nothing, for a cohort explicitly including neonates.

Consistency: 14 passed, 7 failed, 10 warnings; 19 issues recorded. Notable credit to the record: it refuses to invent a reviewing IRB and says so in its own `source_caveats`, which is why the gap is visible at all.
